chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servants, and He is more Knowing of what is in the breasts, more Seeing of what is in the eyes, closer to what is in the bellies, and more Capable of what He wills. Nothing escapes Him, He is not heedless of anything, He does not forget anything, and nothing is hidden from Him. He does not stray from the truth, nor deviate from the correct path, nor does He change, nor is He replaced, nor does He move, nor perish, nor decay, nor be destroyed, nor die—except Allah, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. There is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and there is no god but He, Lord of the Magnificent Throne.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and eternity in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to establish the theological foundation of divine justice (*Adl*) and omniscience, countering early sects that questioned God's attributes. The text underscores that Allah’s knowledge encompasses both the apparent and the hidden, reinforcing His eternal self-subsistence (*Al-Qayyum*) and absolute sovereignty over the Great Throne (*Al-Arsh*). This serves as a critical proof for the Imamate, as the All-Knowing Lord appoints guides who share in His divine knowledge.
